docs.title: Azure DevOps work item payloads
docs.text:
SDO uses Azure DevOps JSON Patch requests when it creates or updates work items. This is an Azure DevOps API requirement and is unrelated to tool manifest formats; SDO supports YAML tool manifests only.

The implementation is in AzureDevOpsClient.cs.

docs.title: Create a work item
docs.text:
Azure DevOps expects a POST request with a JSON Patch array:

POST https://dev.azure.com/{organization}/{project}/_apis/wit/workitems/${type}?api-version=7.1
Content-Type: application/json-patch+json

[
  { "op": "add", "path": "/fields/System.Title", "value": "Example issue title" },
  { "op": "add", "path": "/fields/System.Description", "value": "Description" },
  { "op": "add", "path": "/fields/Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria", "value": "- AC1\n- AC2" }
]

The acceptance-criteria operation is included only when the project supports the Microsoft.VSTS.Common.AcceptanceCriteria field. SDO discovers the available work-item fields from the Azure DevOps work-item type schema.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Set AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT or configure the Azure DevOps credential in Windows Credential Manager. The PAT needs permission to read and write work items.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
• 401 Unauthorized: Check AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT, Credential Manager, and PAT permissions.
  • 400 Bad Request: Check the work-item type, field reference names, and required fields.
  • 404 Not Found: Check the organization, project, and work-item endpoint.

docs.title: Build types
docs.text:
SDO provides two standard build targets:

  • stage creates a package for testing.
  • prod creates a package for release.

docs.title: Stage
docs.text:
sdo stage

The stage target cleans the solution, updates the stage version tag, builds and tests the solution, copies the artifacts, and creates the package.

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
sdo prod

The production target cleans the solution, pulls the latest changes, updates the production version tag, builds and tests the solution, copies the artifacts, and creates the package.

Version increments are documented in versioning.md. GitHub release behavior is documented in github-release.md.

Projects can add custom targets in sdo.targets. See the target reference for the available build targets.

docs.title: Code coverage
docs.text: SDO collects .NET test coverage and generates HTML, Cobertura, and text reports through its build targets.

docs.title: Run coverage
docs.text:
Run tests and collect coverage:

sdo TEST

Generate reports from the test results:

sdo COVERAGE

Display the text summary:

sdo COVERAGE_SUMMARY

COVERAGE requires test results. Run sdo TEST first unless a stage build has already run the tests. sdo STAGE includes testing, report generation, and the coverage summary.

docs.title: Configure coverage
docs.text:
Coverage is enabled by default. Set these MSBuild properties in the project file to change the behavior:

<PropertyGroup>
  <EnableCodeCoverage>true</EnableCodeCoverage>
  <CoverageAssemblyFilters>+MyProject*;-*Tests*;-*Mock*</CoverageAssemblyFilters>
  <CoverageClassFilters>+*;-*.Tests.*;-*.Mocks.*</CoverageClassFilters>
</PropertyGroup>

Filters use + to include, - to exclude, * as a wildcard, and semicolons to separate patterns.

Disable coverage for a faster test run:

sdo TEST -p:EnableCodeCoverage=false

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The report location is the configured CoverageFolder, normally:

<artifacts>\CoverageReport\<version>\

Open index.html for the detailed report. Summary.txt contains the text summary, and coverage.cobertura.xml is copied to the repository root for CI workflows.

Report generation installs the dotnet-reportgenerator-globaltool tool when it is not already available.

docs.title: Executable Details
docs.text:
sdo.exe (Simple DevOps Operations Tool)

  • Purpose: Unified CLI utility for end-to-end build automation, repository management, work item tracking, and pipeline operations across Azure DevOps and GitHub.
  • Key Capabilities:
  • Build & Utility Automation: MSBuild integration, tool management (install/uninstall), environment setup, and GitHub release creation.
  • Work Item Management: Full CRUD operations and commenting on Azure DevOps work items and GitHub issues.
  • Repository & PR Operations: Multi-platform repo creation and deletion, git tagging/branching, and PR creation with branch-based auto-detection.
  • Pipeline Management: CI/CD pipeline creation, execution, and monitoring.
  • Advanced Automation: Auto-discovering YAML configuration system, Markdown parser for rich content generation, and dry-run mode.

docs.title: sdo (Simple DevOps Operations Tool) - Architecture & Design
Overview
docs.text: sdo is a .NET/C# command-line tool for work item creation and repository management across Azure DevOps and GitHub platforms. It provides comprehensive DevOps capabilities with high performance and native .NET ecosystem integration.

docs.title: Architecture Principles
docs.text: All SDO components follow consistent design principles:

docs.title: 1. Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
• CLI Layer: User interaction and command handling
  • Business Logic: Domain-specific orchestration and validation
  • Platform Layer: Platform-specific implementations with abstract interfaces
  • Service Layer: High-level business operations

docs.title: 2. Strategy Pattern
docs.text:
• Abstract platform interfaces enable seamless switching between DevOps platforms
  • Platform-specific implementations handle unique API requirements
  • Consistent interfaces across all supported platforms

docs.title: 3. Extensibility
docs.text:
• Plugin-style architecture for adding new platforms
  • Modular service systems for different business domains
  • Configurable authentication and API integration

docs.title: Advanced Automation Features
docs.text: Advanced Automation Features introduces comprehensive enterprise capabilities to the SDO CLI tool, enabling teams to standardize operations and ensure reliable cross-platform testing.

docs.title: 1. YAML Configuration System
docs.text:
• ConfigurationManager: New utility class with YamlDotNet integration
  • Auto-Discovery: Searches current directory → .temp subfolder → parent directory's .temp folder
  • Nested Structure: Supports complex nested YAML configurations flattened to dot-notation
  • Configuration Priority (highest to lowest):
  • CLI parameters (e.g., sdo wi list --state "Done")
  • Config file defaults (from sdo-config.yaml)
  • Hard-coded defaults in code
  • Example: sdo wi list --config .\.temp\sdo-config.yaml applies default filters for area, state, type, iteration, and top
  • Benefits: Team standardization, reduced repetitive CLI arguments, config file sharing via version control

docs.title: 2. Markdown Parser
docs.text:
• MarkdownParser: New utility class for parsing markdown content
  • Rich Content Support:
  • YAML frontmatter parsing
  • Title and description extraction
  • Metadata extraction (Key: Value format in headers)
  • Acceptance criteria parsing (checkbox-based lists)
  • Code block extraction and preservation
  • Features:
  • GitHub-flavored markdown (GFM) syntax support
  • HTML sanitization for security
  • Comprehensive error reporting with line numbers
  • Verbose mode for detailed diagnostics
  • Integration: Automatically applied when creating work items or PRs from markdown files
  • Benefits: Professional-formatted work items, template reuse, standardized content structure

docs.title: 4. Service Enhancements
docs.text:
• AzureDevOpsClient:
  • Endpoint prioritization: /connectionData first (most reliable), falls back to Graph API
  • Enhanced error handling and logging
  • Improved user detection reliability
  • GitHubClient:
  • Enhanced error handling for API operations
  • Improved API timeout management (default 30s, configurable)
  • Better exception messaging for troubleshooting
  • WorkItemCommand:
  • Comprehensive error handling for list, show, create operations
  • Config file loading with error validation
  • Better user feedback and validation
  • PullRequestCommand:
  • Branch-based auto-detection: extracts work item ID from branch name pattern <number>-<description>
  • Auto-constructs file path as .temp/<work-item-id>-pr-message.md when not provided
  • Supports explicit overrides for file path and work item ID
  • Enhanced error messages with format examples and current branch context
  • Branch existence validation before creation
  • Improved error messages and diagnostic information
  • Benefits: Simplified PR creation workflow, better error handling, improved reliability, enhanced developer experience

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Platform Support: Works seamlessly with Azure DevOps and GitHub
  • Work Item Management: Create, list, show, update, and comment on work items
  • Repository Operations: Create, list, delete, and manage repositories
  • Pull Request Management: Create (with branch-based auto-detection), list, show, and update pull requests
  • Pipeline Management: Create, run, monitor, and manage CI/CD pipelines
  • Dry-Run Mode: Preview operations before execution
  • Automatic Platform Detection: Detects platform from Git remote configuration
  • Branch-Based PR Creation: Auto-detects work item ID and file path from branch name pattern
  • Configuration Management: YAML-based defaults for standardized operations (Advanced Automation Features)
  • Rich Content: Markdown templates for professional work items and PRs (Advanced Automation Features)

docs.text:
• Build and test .NET solutions with sdo solution, sdo clean, and sdo test.
  • Run YAML workflows with sdo run.
  • Install, update, inspect, download, and uninstall tools from apps.yaml.
  • Create GitHub releases and upload release assets.
  • Manage Git repositories, branches, tags, pull requests, and work items.
  • Work with GitHub and Azure DevOps using one command-line interface.
  • Preview supported operations with --dry-run and diagnose them with --verbose.

For commands and options, see the CLI reference. For setup, see usage.

docs.title: GitHub releases
docs.text: SDO creates GitHub releases from the packages produced by the stage and prod build targets. See buildtypes.md for package creation and sdo-net.md for the complete CLI reference.

docs.title: Release targets
docs.text:
Run these targets from a GitHub Actions workflow:

sdo GITHUB_PRE_RELEASE
sdo GITHUB_RELEASE
  • GITHUB_PRE_RELEASE publishes the stage package as a prerelease.
  • GITHUB_RELEASE publishes the production package as a release.

Release packages use this name:

$(SolutionName)-$(ProductVersion).zip

Production releases remove older stage releases. Release notes are generated from commits since the previous matching tag.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Set API_GITHUB_KEY in GitHub Actions or in the local PowerShell session:

$env:API_GITHUB_KEY = "ghp_..."

GitHub CLI authentication is also supported locally:

gh auth login
gh auth status

For GitHub Actions:

- name: Create release
  shell: pwsh
  run: sdo GITHUB_RELEASE
  env:
    API_GITHUB_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_GITHUB_KEY }}
    OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}

Public repositories need authentication for write operations. Private repositories need authentication for all operations. The token must be able to read repository metadata and create releases and assets. For a classic token, use the repo scope.

docs.title: Private release assets
docs.text:
Tool manifests are YAML files. Reference a GitHub release asset with its download URL:

WebDownloadFile: "https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY/releases/download/TAG/asset.zip"

If a private asset URL returns 404, SDO retries through the GitHub API using the configured token. Verify the repository, tag, asset name, and credentials.

docs.title: NbuildTasks
docs.text: NbuildTasks is the MSBuild task library used by SDO build targets. It is included in the solution as NbuildTasks.dll.

docs.title: Available tasks
docs.text:
Task Use RedError Write an error message in red. Git Read or update Git tags. ColorMessage Write a colored message. FileVersion Read a file version. WebDownload Download a file. UnZip Extract a ZIP archive. Zip Create a ZIP archive. Pwsh Run a PowerShell script.

The tasks are registered by common.targets.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Display a colored message:

<Target Name="BUILD_MESSAGE">
  <ColorMessage Message="Build complete" Color="Green" />
</Target>

Read a Git tag:

<Target Name="TAG">
  <Git Command="GetTag" Branch="$(Branch)" BuildType="$(BuildType)">
    <Output TaskParameter="Tag" PropertyName="Tag" />
  </Git>
  <Message Text="Tag: $(Tag)" Importance="high" />
</Target>

Download a file:

<Target Name="DOWNLOAD">
  <WebDownload
    WebUri="https://example.com/archive.zip"
    FileName="$(IntermediateOutputPath)archive.zip" />
</Target>

Run PowerShell:

<Target Name="SCRIPT">
  <Pwsh
    Script="$(SolutionDir)scripts\build\custom-script.ps1"
    Arguments="--example true"
    NoProfile="true"
    ExecutionPolicy="Bypass" />
</Target>

For publishing and installation workflows, use the sdo-scripts module. For the targets that consume these tasks, see the target reference.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: sdo (Simple DevOps Operations) is a C# CLI tool that unifies Azure DevOps, GitHub, and local build workflows. It: - Automatically detects your platform from Git remote configuration - Translates work item states and operations between GitHub and Azure DevOps - Maps sdo commands to native platform CLIs for reference and learning - Provides consistent tooling for teams

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
GitHub: - Install GitHub CLI: gh auth login - Or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable - Or store credentials in Windows Credential Manager under gh:github.com:

Azure DevOps: - Set AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT environment variable (Personal Access Token) - Or store credentials in Windows Credential Manager under GitAzureDevOps - PAT must have scopes: Work Item Read, Code Read

docs.text:
The tool auto-detects your platform from Git remote: - GitHub: https://github.com/owner/repo - Azure DevOps: https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo

git remote -v
# origin https://github.com/naz-hage/sdo (fetch) -> Uses GitHub
# origin  https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo (fetch)  -> Uses Azure DevOps

docs.title: wi: Work item management
docs.text:
Create, list, show, update work items, add comments, and start work. Supports GitHub issues and Azure DevOps work items with automatic state translation.

Subcommands: - list — List work items with filtering - show — Display work item details - create — Create new work item from markdown file (auto-detects .temp\wi.md) - start — Start work on a work item by creating a feature branch (auto-detects work item ID) - update — Update work item properties - comment — Add comment to work item

Help: 

$ sdo wi --help

Description:
  Work item management commands

Usage:
  sdo wi [command] [options]

Commands:
  comment  Add comment to a work item
  create   Create a new work item
  list     List work items with optional filtering
  show     Display detailed work item information
  start    Start work on a work item by creating a feature branch and PR template
  update   Update work item properties

docs.title: wi list
docs.text:
List work items with optional filtering. By default, shows active items (excludes closed/done).

Usage: 

sdo wi list                                    # List active items
sdo wi list --top 20                           # Limit to 20 items
sdo wi list --state Done                       # Show Done items
sdo wi list --state "In Progress" --top 10    # Show In Progress, limit 10
sdo wi list --assigned-to user@example.com    # Filter by assignee
sdo wi list --assigned-to-me                  # Your items
sdo wi list --type PBI                         # Filter by type (Azure DevOps)
sdo wi list --area "Project\Area"             # Filter by area (Azure DevOps)

Context-Aware Next Steps:

Options: - -f, --file-path <file-path> — Path to markdown file containing work item details (optional; defaults to .temp\wi.md if not provided) - --dry-run — Parse and preview work item creation without creating it - --verbose — Show mapping and diagnostics

docs.title: wi close
docs.text:
Close a work item and delete the feature branch. Auto-detects work item ID from the current branch name. Performs git operations: checkout main, pull latest, and delete feature branch.

Usage: 

sdo wi close                         # Auto-detect ID from branch name and close
sdo wi close 243                     # Close with explicit ID
sdo wi close --verbose               # Show detailed output during close
sdo wi close 243 --verbose           # Close with explicit ID and verbose output

Auto-Detection:

When no ID argument is provided: - If on main branch: Requires explicit ID (e.g., sdo wi close 123) - If on feature branch: Extracts ID from branch name (e.g., 123-feature-name → ID 123)

What it does: 1. Validates the work item exists on the current platform (GitHub or Azure DevOps) 2. Checks out the main branch 3. Pulls the latest changes from main 4. Deletes the feature branch locally

Options: - <id> — Work item ID (optional; auto-detected from branch name if not on main) - --verbose — Show detailed output including validation and execution phases

Example Workflow: 

# 1. Start work on issue 243
sdo wi start 243
# Creates branch: 243-issue-description

# 2. Work on the feature...
# (make changes, commit, create PR, merge)

# 3. Close the work item and clean up
sdo wi close
# Auto-detects ID 243 from branch name
# Checks out main
# Pulls latest
# Deletes 243-issue-description branch

Branch Name Format: - Expected format: <number>-<description> - Examples: - ✓ 244-issue → Work item ID 244 - ✓ 123-feature-name → Work item ID 123 - ✗ feature → Error (no number found)

docs.title: repo: Repository management
docs.text:
Create, delete, list, inspect, clone, and tag repositories, and manage Git branches.

Subcommands: - branch — Delete selected local and remote Git branches - list — List repositories - info — Display current Git branch, tag, and remote repository information - clone — Clone a Git repository - tag — Set, auto-create, push, or delete Git tags - create — Create new repository - delete — Delete repository

Help: 

$ sdo repo --help

Description:
  Repository management commands

Usage:
  sdo repo [command] [options]

Commands:
  create <name>  Create a new repository
  delete         Delete a repository
  list           List repositories
  info           Display local Git and remote repository information
  clone          Clone a Git repository
  tag            Git tag operations

An unmatched single token is treated as an MSBuild target, preserving the legacy target-invocation behavior:

sdo build                         # Display available targets
sdo TEST --verbose                # Build the `TEST` target through MSBuild

The target is resolved from sdo.targets in the current directory. Multiple unmatched tokens and unknown options return an error.

docs.title: repo info
docs.text:
sdo repo info
sdo repo info --verbose

repo info combines the local Git branch, project/tag details, and repository metadata from the current Git remote. Use --dry-run to display the local information without contacting the hosting service.

docs.title: repo branch
docs.text:
Manage local and remote Git branches. The current branch, main, and master are always protected.

sdo repo branch --list
sdo repo branch --list --local
sdo repo branch --list --remote
sdo repo branch --delete --name feature-123
sdo repo branch --delete --contains 123

Options: - --list — List branches; defaults to both local and remote branches - --local — With --list, show local branches only - --remote — With --list, show remote branches only - --delete — Delete matching local and remote branches - --name <name> — Select one branch by exact name - --contains <text> — Select branches whose names contain the supplied text - --verbose — Show detailed Git command output

When --contains is used, SDO always prompts for an explicit yes confirmation before deleting any matching branches. Declining the prompt leaves all branches unchanged.

sdo repo clone --url https://github.com/owner/repository --path C:\work\repository

sdo repo tag auto -b stage --dry-run
sdo repo tag push-auto --buildtype stage --dry-run

docs.title: Local automation
docs.text: These command groups consolidate the local build, backup, and file-search workflows into SDO.

docs.title: tool list
docs.text:
Display each application's installed version, manifest version, latest stable release, and upstream link:

sdo tool list
sdo tool list --manifest .\dev-setup\apps.yaml

The command always reports the manifest path it uses, whether the path was provided explicitly or discovered automatically.

Options: - --manifest <path> (-m only) — Optional YAML manifest path; otherwise the current directory, the executable directory, and the default installation directory are searched - --name <name> (-n) — Restrict the table to one application name - --appversion <version> (-av) — Restrict the table to one manifest version - --verbose — Enable detailed output

Latest-version discovery does not require an additional manifest property when WebDownloadFile points directly to a GitHub release download URL. For tools whose download URL is hosted elsewhere, add the optional LatestVersionUrl property to the application entry. This lets SDO use the GitHub repository for version discovery while preserving WebDownloadFile as the download URL. Most applications therefore do not need this property; Helm uses it because its archives are hosted at get.helm.sh.

docs.title: tool manifest update --latest
docs.text:
Update the selected YAML tool manifest with the latest stable version for each application without installing or downloading anything:

sdo tool manifest update --latest
sdo tool manifest update --manifest .\dev-setup\apps.yaml --latest
sdo tool manifest update --name "Python" --latest --dry-run

When --manifest (-m) is omitted, SDO searches for apps.yaml in the current directory, the executable directory, and the default installation directory. All applications are updated by default; use --name (-n) to limit the maintenance action to one application. Use --dry-run (-dr) to preview version changes without modifying the manifest. This command updates the manifest only and does not install, uninstall, or download applications. Applications whose latest version cannot be resolved are reported separately; the dry run still displays all other available changes and leaves the manifest unchanged. Unresolved applications are warnings and do not prevent the command from reporting the manifest as up to date when no resolvable changes remain.

docs.title: tool install --latest
docs.text:
Install a named tool using the latest discovered release:

sdo tool install --name "Python" --latest
sdo tool install --name "Python" --latest --manifest .\dev-setup\apps.yaml
sdo tool install --name "Python" --latest --dry-run

--name is required with --latest. Use --manifest (-m) to select a specific YAML manifest. --appversion cannot be combined with --latest.

docs.title: tool list columns
docs.text:
The sdo tool list table contains one row for each application in the selected manifest:

Column Meaning Name The application name from the manifest. Installed The installed file version when Windows file metadata provides one. If version metadata is unavailable but the file's SHA-256 matches StoredHash, this displays the manifest version. Otherwise, installed means the configured file or installation directory exists, while not installed means neither was found. Manifest The version configured in the selected manifest. Latest The latest version discovered from the application's release metadata. It displays Unresolved when discovery is not supported or fails. Link The release or download URL used for version discovery and review. GitHub download URLs are displayed as the repository's latest-release page when possible.

tool list colors the status row as follows:

  • Green: The installed version matches the manifest version, including a matching StoredHash fallback.
  • Cyan: The application is not installed.
  • Yellow: The application is installed but has an unknown version or does not match the manifest version.
  • Red: Reserved for command errors rather than normal version differences.

Installed is determined as follows:

  • Applications with valid file-version metadata: Installed displays the version reported by the installed file. The manifest hash is not required for this display.
  • Applications with StoredHash: When the installed file does not expose usable version metadata, SDO calculates its SHA-256 hash. If it matches StoredHash, Installed displays the manifest version. If it does not match, Installed displays installed when the configured file or installation directory exists, or not installed otherwise.

docs.title: tool
docs.text:
Environment tool installation, auditing, and manifest management. Use --manifest for YAML manifests. When it is omitted for a named operation, the command searches the current directory, the executable directory, and the default installation directory for apps.yaml.

Subcommands: - install — Install tools from a manifest or by application name - list — Display installed, manifest, and discovered latest versions - uninstall — Uninstall tools from a manifest or by application name - download — Download tools from a manifest

sdo tool list
sdo tool list --manifest .\dev-setup\apps.yaml
sdo tool install --manifest apps.yaml --dry-run
sdo tool download --manifest apps.yaml --dry-run
sdo tool uninstall --manifest apps.yaml --dry-run
sdo tool install --name "Git for Windows" --appversion 2.51.1 --dry-run
sdo tool manifest update --latest --file-path .\docs\sdo.md

Application manifests contain Version, DownloadPath, and NbuildAppList. Use sdo run for generic workflow YAML; do not pass an apps manifest to it.

tool manifest update --latest can also update a Markdown version table after the manifest is maintained. Use --file-path to specify the Markdown file. The documentation update is skipped in dry-run mode.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
Execute a YAML Launcher workflow manifest:

sdo run
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --stage release
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --step build
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --step-index 2 0

--manifest is optional and defaults to sdo.yaml in the current directory. Workflow YAML supports steps, workingDirectory, variables, execution.timeout in seconds, expected return codes, captured output, and stop-on-error behavior. Use exactly one of --stage, --step, or --step-index to execute a named stage, a uniquely named step, or multiple zero-based step indices in the requested order. Stage names, referenced step names, and indices are validated before execution begins. The command reports completed step counts and returns nonzero when the workflow fails.

Stages are ordered groups of existing step names:

stages:
  - name: release
    steps:
      - clean
      - build
      - publish

docs.title: e2e
docs.text:
Run sdo-launcher YAML test metadata by file, test name, or directory:

sdo e2e --test-case metadata/Test_Validate_AzureDevOps_CreateBugFromMarkdown.yaml
sdo e2e --metadata-path metadata
sdo e2e

Test metadata supports step assertions and extracted variables such as {bug_id}. The command reports each result and aggregate totals. Generic workflows and application manifests should use sdo run or sdo tool.

docs.text:

docs.title: Advanced Automation Features
docs.text: Advanced Automation Features introduces comprehensive enterprise capabilities to standardize operations and ensure reliable testing across GitHub and Azure DevOps platforms.

docs.title: Configuration System (YAML-based)
docs.text: The configuration system allows you to standardize work item queries by storing default filters in a YAML configuration file.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Automatic Discovery: Searches for sdo-config.yaml in:
  • Current working directory
  • .temp subfolder in current directory
  • .temp subfolder in parent directory
  • Configuration Priority (highest to lowest):
  • CLI parameters (e.g., sdo wi list --state "Done")
  • Config file defaults (from sdo-config.yaml)
  • Hard-coded defaults in code
  • Optional: Configuration files are completely optional; all commands work without them

docs.title: Configuration File Format
docs.text:
Create sdo-config.yaml in your project:

commands:
  wi:
    list:
      area_path: "Project\\Warriors"
      state: "To Do,In Progress"
      top: 9

docs.title: Usage Examples
docs.text:
Without Configuration: 

sdo wi list --area "Project\Warriors" --state "To Do,In Progress" --top 9
# Returns: 9 work items from Warriors area in To Do or In Progress states

With Configuration File: 

# Place sdo-config.yaml in .temp\ folder
sdo wi list
# Returns: Same 9 items using defaults from config
# Displays: Config: C:\project\.temp\sdo-config.yaml

Override Configuration Defaults: 

# CLI parameters override config defaults
sdo wi list --state "Done"
# Returns: All work items in Done state (ignores config state filter)

docs.title: Configuration Discovery
docs.text:
The tool automatically searches for configuration files:

# From C:\project\myrepo
sdo wi list
# Searches for config in this order:
# 1. C:\project\myrepo\sdo-config.yaml
# 2. C:\project\myrepo\.temp\sdo-config.yaml  
# 3. C:\project\.temp\sdo-config.yaml

docs.title: Explicit Configuration Path
docs.text:
Specify a custom configuration path:

sdo wi list --config "C:\my-configs\standard.yaml"

docs.title: Supported Configuration Keys
docs.text:
Under commands.wi.list in the YAML file:

Key Azure DevOps GitHub Description area_path ✓ - Area path filter (e.g., "Project\Area\SubArea") state ✓ ✓ State filter: New, Approved, Committed, Done, To Do, In Progress type ✓ - Work item type: PBI, Bug, Task, Spike, Epic iteration ✓ - Iteration filter (e.g., "Project\Sprint 1") top ✓ ✓ Maximum items to return (default: 50)

docs.title: Markdown Parser for Content Creation
docs.text: Create professional work items and pull requests using markdown files with rich formatting support.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Markdown Support: GitHub-flavored markdown (GFM) syntax
  • Metadata: YAML frontmatter for work item properties
  • Rich Content: Support for code blocks, acceptance criteria, tables
  • Error Handling: Detailed error reporting with line numbers
  • Security: HTML sanitization for safe content

docs.title: Markdown Format
docs.text:
Basic Format (required): 

# Work Item Title

This is the description text. 
Supports multiple paragraphs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Criterion 1
- [ ] Criterion 2  
- [x] Criterion 3 (completed)

## Code Examples
```csharp
public void DoSomething()
{
    // Code here
}

**With YAML Frontmatter** (optional):
````markdown
---
work_item_type: PBI
priority: High
assignee: user@example.com
labels: "feature, backend, auth"
target: "azdo"  # azdo or github
---

# Authentication Service Design

Implement OAuth2 integration for secure user authentication...

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OAuth2 provider integrated
- [ ] Token refresh mechanism implemented
- [ ] Session management in place

docs.title: Creating Work Items from Markdown
docs.text:
# Create from markdown file
sdo wi create --file-path work-item.md

# Preview before creating (dry-run)
sdo wi create --file-path work-item.md --dry-run

# Show mapping to native commands
sdo wi create --file-path work-item.md --verbose

docs.title: Supported Metadata
docs.text:
In YAML frontmatter under ---:

Field Type Example Platforms work_item_type string PBI, Bug, Task, Feature, Epic Azure DevOps priority string High, Medium, Low Both assignee email user@example.com Both labels csv "backend, auth, security" GitHub area_path string Project\Team\Component Azure DevOps target string azdo, github Both

docs.title: Metadata via Headers
docs.text:
Alternative to YAML frontmatter using level-2 headers:

# Feature Title

## Type: PBI
## Priority: High
## Assignee: user@example.com

Description here...

docs.title: Parsing Details
docs.text:
The parser extracts:

  1. Title: First H1 header (required)
  2. Frontmatter: YAML between --- markers (optional)
  3. Metadata: Level-2 headers in "Key: Value" format (optional)
  4. Description: All paragraphs before acceptance criteria
  5. Code Blocks: All fenced code blocks with language detection
  6. Acceptance Criteria: Unordered list after "## Acceptance Criteria" header

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
# Verbose mode shows detailed parsing errors
sdo wi create --file-path work-item.md --verbose

# Errors include:
# - Line number and content
# - Specific issue (e.g., "Title is required", "Malformed header")
# - Warnings for minor issues (unclosed code blocks, etc.)

docs.title: Platform Detection Errors
docs.text:
Error: Could not determine GitHub repository from Git remote

Causes: - Git remote not configured - Remote URL doesn't match GitHub or Azure DevOps patterns

Solution: 

# Check remote configuration
git remote -v

# Add missing remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/owner/repo
# or
git remote add origin https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo

docs.title: State Validation Errors
docs.text:
Error: Failed to update work item. Supported states: New, Approved, Committed, Done, To Do, In Progress

Causes: - Invalid state name (typo or casing) - Project has custom state configuration

Solution: 

# Use valid state with exact casing (or lowercase)
sdo wi update --id 170 --state Done          # Correct
sdo wi update --id 170 --state "In Progress"  # Correct
sdo wi update --id 170 --state done           # Also works (case-insensitive)

Valid states: - Azure DevOps: New, Approved, Committed, Done, To Do, In Progress - GitHub: open, closed (auto-translated)

docs.title: Azure DevOps Permissions Errors
docs.text:
Error: Unauthorized. Insufficient permissions.

Causes: - PAT token doesn't have required scopes - Work items feature disabled in project

Solution:

Ensure PAT has these scopes: - Work Item > Read - Code > Read

For write operations: - Work Item > Write - Code > Write

# Create new PAT with required scopes
# https://dev.azure.com/org/_usersSettings/tokens

docs.title: Common Option Mistakes
docs.text:
Using invalid option names: 

# ❌ Wrong
sdo wi list --assigned-to-me-filter

# ✓ Correct
sdo wi list --assigned-to-me

Forgetting required flags: 

# ❌ Missing --id for show
sdo wi show

# ✓ Correct
sdo wi show --id 243

Mixing GitHub and Azure DevOps states: 

# ❌ GitHub state on Azure DevOps repo
git remote set-url origin https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo
sdo wi update --id 243 --state closed  # Won't work

# ✓ Correct
sdo wi update --id 243 --state Done

docs.title: sdo-scripts PowerShell module
docs.text:
The sdo-scripts module provides the PowerShell functions used by SDO build and CI workflows.

Source:

scripts/module-package/sdo-scripts.psm1

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Import the module from a repository checkout:

Import-Module .\scripts\module-package\sdo-scripts.psm1 -Force
Get-SdoScriptsVersion
Get-Command -Module sdo-scripts | Sort-Object Name

Install the latest stable SDO release:

Install-Sdo

Install a specific release:

Install-Sdo -Version "1.29.7" -DownloadsDirectory "C:\MyDownloads"

The module is also installed by the SDO build and GitHub Actions workflows.

docs.title: Exported functions
docs.text:
The public API is defined by FunctionsToExport in scripts/module-package/sdo-scripts.psd1.

Function Purpose Publish-AllProjects Build and publish non-test projects. Get-SdoScriptsVersion Return the module version. Set-DevelopmentEnvironment Set local development environment variables. Get-VersionFromYaml Read version fields from an sdo.yaml file. Write-TestResult Write a standardized test result. Test-TargetExists Check whether an MSBuild target exists. Test-TargetDependencies Validate MSBuild target dependencies. Test-TargetDelegation Verify target delegation used by SDO. Get-FileHash256 Compute a SHA-256 file hash. Get-FileVersionInfo Read file and product version metadata. Invoke-FastForward Fast-forward a Git ref. Write-OutputMessage Write consistently formatted output. Get-SdoFileVersion Read the SDO product version from a binary. Add-DeploymentPathToEnvironment Add a deployment path to PATH. Invoke-SdoDownload Download an SDO release artifact. Get-LatestSdoReleaseVersion Find the latest stable SDO release. Install-Sdo Install an SDO release.

View the installed commands at any time:

Get-Command -Module sdo-scripts

docs.title: Build and CI usage
docs.text:
Publish projects with an explicit repository path:

Publish-AllProjects `
  -OutputDir C:\Artifacts `
  -Version 1.0.0 `
  -RepositoryRoot C:\MyRepo

Run target validation:

Test-TargetDelegation -SolutionDir .

The PUBLISH target uses Publish-AllProjects. The SMOKE_TEST target uses Test-TargetDelegation.

Example GitHub Actions setup:

- name: Install SDO
  shell: pwsh
  run: |
    Import-Module ./scripts/module-package/sdo-scripts.psm1 -Force
    Install-Sdo

docs.title: Install SDO
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install the latest stable SDO release:

git clone https://github.com/naz-hage/sdo.git
Set-Location .\sdo
Import-Module .\scripts\module-package\sdo-scripts.psm1 -Force
Install-Sdo

Install a specific release with -Version:

Install-Sdo -Version "1.74.0"

Verify the installation:

sdo --help
sdo --version

For module functions and CI usage, see sdo-scripts-module.md.

docs.title: Overview of dev-setup Folder
docs.text:
The dev-setup folder typically includes the following files:

  • sdo.yaml
    • Contains installation information for SDO. This file is required to install SDO before other development tools.
  • apps.yaml
    • Lists the development tools required for your project, including their installation and uninstallation details.
  • Legacy scripts (deprecated in favor of sdo-scripts module)
  • Individual PowerShell scripts for specific tasks

docs.title: 1. sdo.yaml
docs.text:
This file provides the installation details for SDO, which is required to manage other tools in the project.

Example: 

Version: "1.2.0"
NbuildAppList:
  - Name: "sdo"
    Version: "1.7.0"
    AppFileName: "$(InstallPath)\\sdo.exe"
    WebDownloadFile: "https://github.com/naz-hage/sdo/releases/download/$(Version)/$(Name)-$(Version).zip"
    DownloadedFile: "$(Name)-$(Version).zip"
    InstallCommand: "powershell.exe"
    InstallArgs: "-Command Expand-Archive -Path $(DownloadedFile) -DestinationPath '$(InstallPath)' -Force"
    InstallPath: "$(ProgramFiles)\\sdo"
    UninstallCommand: "powershell.exe"
    UninstallArgs: "-Command Remove-Item -Path '$(InstallPath)' -Recurse -Force"
    StoredHash: "XXX"
    AddToPath: true

docs.title: 2. apps.yaml
docs.text:
This file lists all the development tools required for the project. Each tool is defined with its name, version, installation details, and uninstallation details.

Example: 

Version: "1.2.0"
NbuildAppList:
  - Name: "7-zip"
    Version: "23.01"
    AppFileName: "$(InstallPath)\\7z.exe"
    WebDownloadFile: "https://www.7-zip.org/a/7z2301-x64.exe"
    DownloadedFile: "7zip.exe"
    InstallCommand: "$(DownloadedFile)"
    InstallArgs: "/S /D=\"$(ProgramFiles)\\7-Zip\""
    InstallPath: "$(ProgramFiles)\\7-Zip"
    UninstallCommand: "$(InstallPath)\\Uninstall.exe"
    UninstallArgs: "/S"

Key Elements in apps.yaml:

Element Name Description Name The name of the tool. Version The version of the tool. AppFileName The file name of the tool, used to check if it is already installed. WebDownloadFile The URL to download the tool. LatestVersionUrl (Optional) URL used by tool list to discover the latest stable release when the download URL is not a GitHub release URL. LatestVersionStrategy (Optional) Provider-specific discovery strategy, such as github-tags, mongodb-download-page, or docker-appcast. DownloadedFile The name of the downloaded file, used for installation. InstallCommand The command to install the tool. InstallArgs The arguments for the installation command. InstallPath The location where the tool will be installed. UninstallCommand The command to uninstall the tool. UninstallArgs The arguments for the uninstallation command. UpdateInPlace (Optional) Updates the tool without uninstalling the existing installation first. Use this for installers that support in-place upgrades, such as Docker Desktop. StoredHash (Optional) SHA256 hash of the file for verification and version reporting when the file has no version metadata. AddToPath (Optional) Whether to add the tool's path to the system PATH environment variable.

LatestVersionUrl is not required for normal installation or for tools that use a pinned manifest version. The tool list command can discover a release automatically when WebDownloadFile is a GitHub release download URL. Add LatestVersionUrl only when the download host is different from the release host, such as Helm:

- Name: "Helm"
  Version: "3.21.3"
  WebDownloadFile: "https://get.helm.sh/helm-v$(Version)-windows-amd64.zip"
  LatestVersionUrl: "https://github.com/helm/helm"

In this example, Helm releases are discovered from GitHub while the actual archive continues to download from get.helm.sh. The value should identify the GitHub repository (https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY); it is not required to include a version or release tag.

docs.title: 3. dev-setup.ps1
docs.text:
This PowerShell script automates the installation of tools and sets up the development environment.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Installs the latest stable SDO release ending in .0.
  • Installs other tools listed in apps.yaml .
  • Verifies administrative privileges before proceeding.

Example: 

# Import the install module
$url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/naz-hage/sdo/main/dev-setup/install.psm1"
$output = "./install.psm1"
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $output
Import-Module ./install.psm1 -Force

# Install SDO
Install-Sdo
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-OutputMessage "Error: Installation of SDO failed. Exiting script."
    exit 1
}

# Install other tools
& $global:NbExePath install --manifest .\apps.yaml
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
    Write-OutputMessage "Error: Installation of other tools failed. Exiting script."
    exit 1
}

Write-OutputMessage "Completed installation script."

docs.title: Folder Structure
docs.text:
Your project folder should look like this: 

%MainDirectory%\
├── MyProject\
│   ├── dev-setup\
│   │   ├── sdo.yaml
│   │   ├── apps.yaml
│   │   ├── dev-setup.ps1
│   ├── ... other project and test files
│   └── sdo.targets  (this file is required in the solution folder)

docs.title: Adding a New Development Tool
docs.text:
To add a new tool to your project: 1. Identify the tool's: - Download URL and file name. - Installation and uninstallation commands and arguments. - Installation path. - File name for version checks. - Version and name. 2. Add the tool's details to apps.yaml.

Example for a new tool: 

Name: "Docker"
Version: "4.38.0.0"
AppFileName: "$(InstallPath)\\Docker Desktop.exe"
WebDownloadFile: "https://desktop.docker.com/win/main/amd64/Docker%20Desktop%20Installer.exe"
DownloadedFile: "Docker Desktop Installer.exe"
InstallCommand: "$(DownloadedFile)"
InstallArgs: "install --quiet"
InstallPath: "$(ProgramFiles)\\Docker\\Docker"
UninstallCommand: "powershell.exe"
UninstallArgs: "-Command \"Remove-Item -Path '$(InstallPath)' -Recurse -Force\""
AddToPath: true

docs.title: SDO Usage
docs.text: SDO provides the sdo command-line tool for build automation, YAML workflows, tool management, and DevOps operations.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Install the .NET SDK.
  • Install SDO and open a Developer Command Prompt for Visual Studio.
  • Change to the solution or repository directory.

docs.title: First Run
docs.text:
Build and clean the current solution:

sdo solution
sdo clean

Run unit tests with the repository target or dotnet test:

sdo TEST
dotnet test

Use --verbose for diagnostic output and --dry-run to preview supported operations.

docs.title: YAML Workflows
docs.text:
The YAML command families have separate purposes:

  • sdo run [--manifest <file>] runs a YAML Launcher workflow. The default manifest is sdo.yaml in the current directory.
  • sdo tool <operation> --manifest <file> manages YAML tool manifests.
  • sdo e2e --test-case <path-or-name> runs test metadata with assertions.

To execute a named stage or selected steps, use exactly one selection option:

sdo run
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --stage release
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --step build
sdo run --manifest workflow.yaml --step-index 2 0

--stage executes a named, ordered group of step names. --step executes one uniquely named step. --step-index accepts multiple zero-based indices and preserves their requested order. Stage names, referenced step names, and indices are validated before any selected step starts. These options are mutually exclusive.

Stages are defined beside the top-level steps collection:

stages:
  - name: release
    steps:
      - clean
      - build
      - publish

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
See the sdo CLI reference for all commands, options, examples, configuration, build targets, and troubleshooting guidance.

  • SDO targets
  • Code coverage

docs.title: Versioning and automation
docs.text:
SDO uses X.Y.Z versions for binaries, products, and repository tags:

Part Changes when X A breaking change is released. Y A feature or fix is released, or a production build is deployed. Incrementing Y resets Z to 0. Z A staging build is deployed.

Tags identify repository versions, associate release assets, and generate release notes from commits since the previous tag. See buildtypes.md for staging and production builds and github-release.md for release behavior.

docs.title: Update tool versions
docs.text:
Tool versions are maintained in dev-setup/apps.yaml. Update the manifest and a Markdown version table with:

sdo tool manifest update --latest --file-path .\docs\sdo.md

The command discovers the latest stable releases, updates the YAML manifest, and synchronizes matching tool/version rows in the selected Markdown file. Use --dry-run to preview changes.

docs.title: Read the SDO version
docs.text:
Import-Module "./scripts/module-package/sdo-scripts.psm1" -Force
$version = Get-VersionFromYaml -YamlPath "./dev-setup/sdo.yaml"

The Markdown synchronization is implemented by Sdo/Services/UpdateVersionsInDocs.cs and invoked by sdo tool manifest update.
